name: story/explainer
summary: One idea made to land as a narrated motion explainer: kit shapes on one stage, moved beat by beat by kit verbs, with the browser voice reading each beat and a caption under it.
not_for: a written explainer with no motion (use story)

slots.name: title
slots.says: page title, the idea in a few words

slots.name: headline
slots.says: H1, the one idea stated as a finding

slots.name: dek
slots.says: one or two sentences: what the explainer shows, and that you press Play

slots.name: engine
slots.says: the kit-engine script, copied verbatim from the reference artifact the tunnel-a-story skill names; never edited

slots.name: parts
slots.says: var lines that make every part with kit shapes (S.path, S.label, S.dimension, S.group ...), each with k:'<name>' so a review mark can sit on it

slots.name: beats
slots.says: one {say:'...', do:function(t){...}} per beat: one spoken sentence, and kit verbs only (show, hide, draw, up, move, color, pulse, morph, rise)

slots.name: takeaway
slots.says: the one line the reader should keep, under the player

finish_line.says: one H1, and it states the finding
links a kit tunnel holds (kit v2: kit.css and kit.js), so it renders in every viewer
no stylesheet or script from another host (the kit is ours)
every slot filled, the engine pasted in
carries the kit engine and a separate beats script
600 visible words at most: the beats carry the story
the kit-engine script is the pinned reference, unedited
the beats call only kit shapes and verbs: no timers, requestAnimationFrame or animate() of their own
every part has a k name, one word per thing, the same name throughout
no dashed strokes on parts: dashed means a region in review
every say is one sentence the voice can read: numbers and units written as spoken
works at 400px wide, in dark mode, and with reduced motion (end states only)
says whether it has been played in Safari in the app; an unplayed explainer says so
